headline: Post-NVIDIA spike round-trips and stabilises mid-range: Tail stays low, Stress elevated into the U.S. data block
body: Nasdaq-100 September futures trade at 29,538.75, up 249.25 points or 0.85%, as of 02:15Z. The overnight range runs from 29,432.50 to 29,654.75, and price now sits close to the middle of it. That is the central observation of this assessment: the post-earnings spike high was retraced by roughly two thirds toward the session low and has since recovered only part of the give-back, which is retracement-rich, two-way price discovery rather than persistent one-way extension. NQ is not holding near a session extreme, no failed retracement has been followed by repeated extension, and the largest single-name catalyst of the cycle has so far produced a round trip. NVIDIA reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106% year over year, non-GAAP earnings of $2.22 per share, a 75.0% gross margin and third-quarter revenue guidance of $108.0 billion plus or minus 2%, with the shares up roughly 4% after hours. Cross-asset context is calm to mildly conflicting. VIX closed at 15.21, down 1.55% at its session low, and VIX futures are a further 0.32% lower overnight. The 2-year Treasury yield is 4.17% and the 10-year near 4.64% on the latest H.15 observation, with Treasury futures marginally bid, so there is no bond-market stress transmission. WTI is $81.57 and Brent $87.26, a fourth consecutive decline on Strait of Hormuz de-escalation hopes after Iran and Oman reached an agreement on their respective waters. That de-escalation is reversible: allied assessments reported on 26 August hold that 80 to 150 mines may still remain despite the claim that the strait has been cleared, and a tanker was struck by a projectile off Oman on 25 August. Gold is consolidating above $4,600. Latest-session internals are genuinely split rather than aligned, with megacaps three up and five down for a mean of -0.22%, a semiconductor basket mean of +0.83% led by ARM at +3.93%, and software-infrastructure up 1.14% against software-application down 0.90%. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction and raise Stress; they are not evidence of index-level mean-reversion failure. The macro backdrop keeps Stress elevated: July core PCE held at 3.3% year over year with headline at 3.7%, leaving the rate path unresolved, and the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Wednesday down 0.17% at 29,995.38 after fading from 30,195.72. The forward path therefore holds Tail in the 10-13 band across the Asian and European hours, lifts it to 17 for the hour containing initial jobless claims at 12:30Z and to 20 and 21 for the cash open and first full cash hour, then decays it back to 11 by the end of the window as post-event discovery is assumed to normalise.

lookbackSummary: Over the preceding 24 hours Claude held Tail in the 10-16 band through the Wednesday European and U.S. sessions, with Stress drifting from 47 up to 61 as the market positioned into July core PCE and the NVIDIA print. Tail stepped to 21 for the 20:00Z hour containing the earnings release, then decayed through 18, 16 and 13 as the initial reaction proved two-sided rather than one-way. Two hourly slots, 21:00Z and 00:00Z, have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forward window holds Tail in the 10-13 band across the Asian and European hours on the observation that the post-earnings round trip left mean reversion available and price is trading mid-range rather than at an extreme. It rises to 17 for the hour containing initial jobless claims at 12:30Z and to 20 and 21 for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours covering the U.S. cash open and the first full hour of cash NVIDIA repricing, the one stretch where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is a credible conditional risk. It then decays through the afternoon to 10 by the quiet pre-Asia hour and 11 at the window close. Stress traces a similar arc from 51 to a 62 peak and back to 44. Scheduled checkpoints inside the window are U.S. jobless claims at 12:30Z, the 13:30Z cash open and the Kansas City Fed Composite Index at 15:00Z; Michigan sentiment final and a Fed Chair Warsh speech follow on 28 August at 14:00Z.
